parseAudit.decision: The old 3-parse-error inventory is retained as historical evidence but does not define the canonical correctness cohort. The later canonical audit records 6 parse errors plus 13 mixed-board exclusions and exactly 8,650 canonical cases.

correctnessPredicate.rule: For a feasible input, correctness means a fresh geometrically/industrially valid plan whose terminal-dimension multiset exactly matches demand under the historical rotation-normalized comparison. A demanded piece that cannot fit the historically usable board in any allowed orientation is expected-infeasible rather than an optimizer regression.
correctnessPredicate.referencePanelsRole: reference_panels / delta is a quality comparison versus Lepton and is reported, but it is not the historical correctness acceptance gate.
evidence: benchmark_project_v10.csv records estado and delta independently.
10 rows are estado=OK with delta>0, so using more boards than Lepton was still accepted as correct.
33 rows are estado=ERROR with delta<=0, so non-worse board count did not make an invalid plan correct.
The 93 ERROR rows split into 33 terminal-dimension multiset failures and 60 physically infeasible inputs; 450 SKIP rows are format-scope exclusions.
Optimizador_V11_Candidato_Prod_Benchmark_Project.html normalizes terminal dimensions as min(width,height) x max(width,height) before multiset comparison.
The same historical benchmark reads trim from the first project root node, defaults it to 10 when missing, and applies the value to refiladoX and refiladoY.

multisetSemantics.reason: The historical benchmark compared the semantic terminal dimensions parsed from the reference and generated project XML; it did not key the acceptance multiset by application metadata.

executionBinding.canonicalParser: current src/lib/optimizer/canonical-xml.ts remains unchanged and defines canonical parsing/identity

historicalValidationCorpus.role: Empirical validation corpus for the historical infeasible classifier. The embedded projection has 2,001 records but exactly 2,000 XML identities; the physical parte1 archive and benchmark both bind those same 2,000 identities.

certificationCorpus.role: Exact Kernel V1 correctness/certification cohort source: 8,669 physical XML, 19 parser exclusions, 8,650 accepted identities.

projectUsableBoard.apply: same trim value to refiladoX and refiladoY

executionBinding.orderUsableBoard: No project-benchmark provenance exists for Order trim; retain the canonical Order binding unchanged.

infeasibleClassification.method: First validate the classifier on the separate physical parte1 benchmark corpus using the historical execution binding, requiring an exact 60/60 filename match. Only after that gate passes, apply the same classifier to the exact physical resto 8,650 cohort.
infeasibleClassification.execution: Expected-infeasible cases in resto count toward correctness classification coverage but are not sent to optimizeProject and are excluded from fullPlanHash determinism denominators.

historicalReplayGate.requirement: All 2,000 benchmark filenames must exist in parte1 and the classifier must reproduce exactly the same 60 historical physically-infeasible filenames before resto classification or calibration may start.
historicalReplayGate.inferenceBoundary: The 60 historical cases validate the classifier on parte1. They do not define, estimate, or constrain the expected-infeasible count in resto.
historicalReplayGate.aggregationRule: Replay is keyed by physical filename. parseCanonicalXml aggregates all project panels into one canonical demand; the filename is expected-infeasible if any demanded piece in that aggregated case cannot fit the historically usable board.

deterministicBudgets.rule: Do not run formal determinism certification with absent, guessed, smoke-test, or CI-convenience budgets. Calibrate each deterministic budget from work/time measured in the exact invocation scope where that parameter is enforced, while separately reporting aggregate per-order work. Watchdog hits must be zero during formal certification.

calibrationProtocol.supersessionReason: v2 used canonical project trim=0 for physical feasibility and a stronger-than-historical application-metadata multiset; its partial checkpoints must not be reused.
calibrationProtocol.historicalReplayCorpus: parte1 validates the infeasible classifier against the exact 60 historical filenames before any resto calibration work.
calibrationProtocol.calibrationCorpus: resto exact 8,650 accepted cohort after current parser exclusions and historical execution binding.
calibrationProtocol.inputSource: physical resto XML parsed through unchanged current canonical parser plus the versioned historical execution binding, after separate parte1 replay validation
calibrationProtocol.initialOrder: work-first with explicit OneBoard discovery from the physical resto cohort: statically filter feasible cases whose historical-execution-binding area lower bound is 1, prioritize referencePanels>1 then larger piece count, reserve up to 48 by default, then continue normal hotspot-driven work-first ordering; known extreme tails remain last. --oneboardScanLimit overrides the static scan size; legacy --oneboardQuota is accepted as an alias. Ordering changes priority only, never the exact 8,650-case universe.
calibrationProtocol.telemetryWiringRule: composition.optimizarCalls, composition.armarPlacasCalls, and composition.stageCalls must be positive for each calibrated run. beamCalls may legitimately be zero when greedy reaches the area lower bound.
calibrationProtocol.telemetryProbeRule: Before calibration, a fresh valid run must show non-zero Beam expansions, Master nodes, or OneBoard attempts. Calls/runs alone do not satisfy the probe. A controlled Beam no-complete-plan fallback is allowed only with valid final output and live Beam work/terminal-control accounting; unexpected Beam exceptions fail the probe.
calibrationProtocol.beamRule: OPTIMIZER_MAX_BEAM_EXPANSIONS is enforced per armarPlacasBeam invocation, so its primary calibration statistic is beam.expansionsMax. beam.expansionsTotal is retained as aggregate per-order load evidence and must not be mistaken for the per-call budget.
calibrationProtocol.aggregateBudgetDecision: Do not add a new aggregate request stop condition inside Kernel V1 freeze. That changes search semantics and requires a new Kernel V1 candidate plus all gates.
calibrationProtocol.promotionRequirement: Version explicit positive integer production values with calibration evidence before formal correctness/determinism certification.
calibrationProtocol.telemetryProbeSelection: Use versioned hotspot rows whose historical metricas.master.activaciones or metricas.oneboard.activaciones is positive. Try the cheapest known activated feasible cases first, up to eight candidates; the current candidate must actually exercise Beam, Master, or OneBoard before calibration starts.
calibrationProtocol.telemetryProbeInterpretation: Historical activation is only candidate-selection evidence. PASS still requires a fresh current run with valid output, live composition telemetry, and at least one current Beam/Master/OneBoard counter greater than zero.
calibrationProtocol.v3Disposition: v3 replay/correctness/timing observations remain useful evidence, but v3 calibration rows are not authoritative for deterministic work-budget derivation because the probe accepted calls without proving non-zero Beam/Master/OneBoard work magnitudes.
calibrationProtocol.beamAccountingRule: When beam.calls > 0, calibration v4 requires Beam work or terminal-control accounting; beam.calls > 0 with expansions/timeout/budget/watchdog all zero is an observability failure and stops calibration.
calibrationProtocol.watchdogEvidenceRule: Calibration runs with budgets/watchdogs OFF; watchdogHits=0 there is not certification evidence. Formal zero-watchdog evidence is collected only after production watchdog values are versioned and enabled.
calibrationProtocol.budgetScopeRule: Primary budget statistics must match enforcement scope: Beam expansionsMax/wallMsMax per Beam invocation; Master nodesMax/wallMsMax per resolverCobertura run; OneBoard attemptsMax/wallMsMax per rescatarUnaPlaca invocation.
calibrationProtocol.aggregateWorkRule: Also report per-order aggregate totals and call/run counts to characterize request-level load. Kernel V1 Candidate A has no aggregate request work budget; adding one changes search semantics and requires a new candidate plus recertification.
calibrationProtocol.samplingRule: Early --maxNew batches are stratified for evidence density: first a bounded physical-resto areaLB=1 OneBoard candidate scan, then hotspot-driven work-first calibration. This changes execution order only; the final certification universe remains the exact feasible subset of the fixed 8,650 resto cohort.
calibrationProtocol.oneboardEvidenceRule: The 213-row hotspot marker has zero historical OneBoard activations and cannot source this evidence. OneBoard discovery starts from the physical resto feasible cohort using cotaArea==1 under the historical execution binding. Static candidacy is not activation evidence: promotion requires fresh current oneboard.runs>0 and attemptsTotal>0. If an adequate static scan yields no activations, document empirical rarity and set the rescue budget by explicit policy rather than inventing a distribution.
calibrationProtocol.benchmarkProfile: benchmarkInputFromCanonicalCase(...,{strategy:"v10"}) defaults to profile=balanced. Historical calibration ceilings are therefore Beam 1500ms (motor default), Master 8000ms, OneBoard 20000ms.
calibrationProtocol.beamFallbackRule: The candidate explicitly degrades Beam to greedy when armarPlacasBeam throws. Calibration accepts only the controlled no-complete-plan error (message starts No se pudo completar el plan con Beam Search) when the final output remains valid and Beam work/terminal-control accounting is present. Any other Beam exception remains a calibration failure.
calibrationProtocol.beamTimeoutInterpretation: Beam timeoutHits is aggregated across Beam invocations. Under the v10 benchmark balanced profile the historical per-invocation Beam ceiling is 1500ms, not 2500ms. A case with timeoutHits>0 contains time-censored Beam work even if other invocations terminate normally.

candidateEvidence.beam: 48 activated cases / 2518 invocations; 47 cases without Beam timeout have expansionsMax p50=20 p90=32 max=1016. 1024 is the first deterministic equivalence candidate and must preserve baseline boardCount on the finite validation cohort.
candidateEvidence.master: 27 resolverCobertura invocations; 22 uncensored (p50=1 p90=1 max=580) and 5 historical-time-censored explosive runs up to 1306553 nodes at ~8s. 1600000 is an explicit reference-equivalence candidate above the observed censored work envelope; it is not claimed to be natural completed-search work.
candidateEvidence.oneboard: 22/22 activated runs; attemptsMax p50=p90=max=384; zero raw timeout hits; 384 is both the structural search-space ceiling and the empirical completed-run maximum.
candidateEvidence.watchdogs: Watchdogs are safety fuses, not work budgets: Beam 5s is above the observed ~1.8s historical-timeout call envelope; Master 60s accommodates 1.6M nodes even near the slowest observed censored throughput (~33k nodes/s); OneBoard 10s is >4x the observed 2.366s completed-run envelope.

candidatePromotionGate.scope: Re-run the already measured calibration checkpoint cases under candidate values; no new statistical sampling is required for promotion.
requirements: validationOk=true and historical demand multiset exact for every case
boardCount exactly equals the budgets-OFF baseline for every re-run case
controlled Beam fallback remains acceptable only under the existing semantic fallback rule
candidatePromotionGate.failureRule: If a case fails, adjust only the budget/watchdog for the path implicated by telemetry and re-run failed cases plus their same-path cohort. Do not restart calibration methodology or expand the runtime-estimation sample.
candidatePromotionGate.successAction: Copy candidateValues into deterministicBudgets.values, set deterministicBudgets.status=RESOLVED, version the evidence, then start formal correctness.

ordering.calibration: work-first stratified: up to 48 physical resto feasible cases with static areaLB=1 first (referencePanels>1, then piece count), then normal hotspot-driven work ordering; known extreme tail last. --oneboardScanLimit overrides scan size; --order cheap-first available. Final universe unchanged.
ordering.correctness: calibration measured wallMs ascending when available

partialCoverage: historical classifier validation: exact 60/60 infeasible filename replay over the 1,550 non-SKIP parte1 benchmark cases
correctness: classified resto cases / 8650, including expected-infeasible classifications
determinism-repeat: repeated feasible plan cases / feasible resto cases
determinism-repeat timing mass: sum of baseline correctness wallMs for repeated feasible cases / total feasible correctness wallMs
calibration: completed feasible v4 resto cases plus separately scoped historical-hotspot timing-mass coverage

blockingReasons: Candidate deterministic budgets/watchdogs require finite baseline-equivalence validation before promotion.
